Certified type:
- Category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument" — the schema examples list categories like "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", etc. This is a non-automatic weighing instrument (NAWI). I'll use "Non-automatic weighing instrument".
- Type designations: DS-983, DS-984
- Variants: ES, FS, BF, BC, RL, SA, SB, SC, RA, RB, PS, PS-B, CD, C — these are variants of the type. Should these be model_family models? The cert covers types DS-983, DS-984 with variants. Hmm. The variants are listed under "Variants:". These could be considered model variants. But model_family should be included ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. There are 2 types (DS-983, DS-984) and 14 variants. I could include model_family with models for the variants. But the characteristics table applies to the whole family (Max 6-30 kg, etc.), not per variant. The schema says model_family: include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. There are multiple variants listed, so include model_family with models: DS-983, DS-984 and possibly variants. I think safest: models for type designations DS-983 and DS-984, with attributes maybe variant list. Actually the variants are sub-variants. Let me include model_family with family_name null and models: [{"model_id": "DS-983"}, {"model_id": "DS-984"}]. The variants could be captured as config_level axis "variant" with conditions. Hmm.

Actually, the characteristics are common across the family (they don't vary per model). The variants (ES, FS, BF, BC, RL, SA, SB, SC, RA, RB, PS, PS-B, CD, C) are configuration variants. I could record them as config_level entries with axis "variant" listing each variant, but values would be... nothing meaningful. Perhaps better to include them in model_family models as variants, or in a matrix? I'll include model_family.models as DS-983 and DS-984, and add config_level with axis "variant" listing conditions? The config_level values require {condition, value}. Value would be null-ish. Maybe better to just note variants in certified_type description or a config_level with attribute "variant" and conditions = variant names, value = true? That seems fabricated.

Alternative: put variants in model_family.models as model_ids like "DS-983 (variant ES)" — that would be 28 entries, fabricated combos. No.

I think best: model_family with models DS-983, DS-984; and characteristics.model_level not needed since attributes don't vary. Actually the schema says model_level for attribute × model matrix. Since Max range 6-30 kg applies to all, it's type_level.

Hmm, but is 6 kg ≤ Max ≤ 30 kg a range across models or a single instrument's range? "Maximum capacity: 6 kg ≤ Max ≤ 30 kg" — this likely means the type family covers Max from 6 kg to 30 kg, i.e., different models have different Max within that range. Could be a matrix. But we don't have per-model data, so keep it as type_level range: {min: 6, max: 30}, unit kg.

Characteristics extraction:
- accuracy_class: "III" (value string "III", unit null)
- maximum_capacity: {min: 6, max: 30} kg
- verification_scale_interval: {min: 1, max: null} g
- weighing_ranges: single and multi-interval — could be two entries: weighing_range_type: "Single interval" and "Multi-interval" — maybe a list string. I'll do a type_level characteristic "weighing_ranges" value "Single interval, Multi-interval"? Hmm, or "single_and_multi_interval". Let me record as value string "Single interval / Multi-interval"? The rules say structured values. Since it's a categorical, string value with unit null is acceptable. I'll do two characteristics? Better one: "weighing_ranges": {value: ["Single interval", "Multi-interval"]}? The schema shape says value: number | {min,max} | string. I'll use string "Single interval / Multi-interval".

- max_scale_intervals_single_range: {max: 3000} divisions (dimensionless). "Maximum number of scale intervals (one weighing range)" n ≤ 3000 divisions → value {min: null, max: 3000}, unit_symbol: "divisions"? Divisions isn't really a unit but I can put unit_symbol null and value 3000 max. The label says "divisions". I'll use unit_symbol null since divisions is dimensionless counting unit; or unit_symbol "divisions". Rules say unit separation; "divisions" could be kept as unit_symbol "divisions" but it's not in unitsdb. I'll set unit_symbol: null and mention divisions via label? Hmm, label max_number_of_scale_intervals_single_range, value {min:null, max:3000}. I think fine. Actually let me use unit_symbol "divisions" — the caller will look up and might not find; rule says leave unit_id null unless certain. unit_symbol can be raw. I'll include "divisions".

- max_scale_intervals_multi_interval: n ≤ 3000 per partial weighing range → {min:null, max:3000}, with note "(per partial weighing range)". I'll include as separate attribute max_number_of_scale_intervals_per_partial_range. Could add footnote? No footnote markers here.

- max_partial_weighing_ranges: 2
- tare: "T ≤ -50% for single interval instrument; T ≤ -Max₁ for multi-interval instrument" — this is config-level! Axis: instrument interval type (single vs multi). So config_level:
  attribute: tare_limit, axis: weighing_range_type
  values: [{condition: "single interval", value: {min:null, max:-50}, unit_symbol: "%"}, {condition: "multi interval", value: "-Max₁", ...}]. Hmm, "T ≤ -Max₁" means tare ≤ negative of Max (initial tare?). Max₁ is max of first partial range. The subscript 1. I'll record value string "-Max1" (avoid subscript char? Max₁ uses unicode subscript; keep as "−Max₁"? Better ASCII "Max1"). Let me use value "-Max1" with unit null and maybe note. Or keep as string "-Max₁". JSON supports unicode. I'll use "-Max₁"? To be safe with "no LaTeX" rule, unicode subscript is fine but might be weird. I'll use "-Max1".

- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40} °C
- power supply: three options — this is config_level! Axis: power supply option.
  - Option 1: 6–12 V DC via plug-in power supply → power_supply_voltage {min:6, max:12} V, power_supply_type DC
  - Option 2: 100–240 V AC 50/60 Hz → voltage {min:100,max:240} V AC, frequency {min:50,max:60} Hz
  - Option 3: 5 V DC via USB
  
  Config_level entries:
  - attribute: power_supply_voltage, axis: power_supply_option
    values: [{condition: "plug-in power supply (DC)", value: {min:6,max:12}, unit_symbol:"V"}, {condition: "mains (AC)", value: {min:100,max:240}, unit_symbol:"V"}, {condition: "USB", value: 5, unit_symbol:"V"}]
  - attribute: power_supply_frequency, axis: power_supply_option, values: [{condition: "mains (AC)", value: {min:50,max:60}, unit_symbol:"Hz"}]
  - attribute: power_supply_type, axis: power_supply_option, values: [{condition: "plug-in power supply", value:"DC"}, {condition:"mains", value:"AC"}, {condition:"USB", value:"DC"}]

  Also type_level power_supply_type could be "DC or AC". I'll rely on config_level.

- application: "Intended to be used for direct sales to the public" → type_level application value string.
- software_identification: "V01.xx (xx = 00 … 99)" → value string "V01.xx (xx = 00 … 99)" or "V01.xx". I'll use "V01.xx (xx = 00…99)".
